personae.name: EGLAMOUR
personae.blurb: agent for Silvia in her escape

personae.name: JULIA
personae.blurb: a lady of Verona, beloved of Proteus

scenes.setting: Verona. An open place

lines.text: Enter Valentine and Proteus.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Cease to persuade, my loving Proteus.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Home-keeping youth have ever homely wits.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Were’t not affection chains thy tender days

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: To the sweet glances of thy honoured love,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: I rather would entreat thy company

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: To see the wonders of the world abroad

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Than, living dully sluggardized at home,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Wear out thy youth with shapeless idleness.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: But since thou lov’st, love still, and thrive therein,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Even as I would when I to love begin.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Wilt thou be gone? Sweet Valentine, adieu.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Think on thy Proteus when thou haply seest

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Some rare noteworthy object in thy travel.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Wish me partaker in thy happiness

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: When thou dost meet good hap; and in thy danger,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: If ever danger do environ thee,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Commend thy grievance to my holy prayers,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: For I will be thy beadsman, Valentine.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: And on a love-book pray for my success?

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Upon some book I love I’ll pray for thee.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: That’s on some shallow story of deep love,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: How young Leander crossed the Hellespont.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: That’s a deep story of a deeper love,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: For he was more than over shoes in love.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: ’Tis true; for you are over boots in love,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: And yet you never swam the Hellespont.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Over the boots? Nay, give me not the boots.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: No, I will not, for it boots thee not.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: What?

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: To be in love, where scorn is bought with groans,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Coy looks with heart-sore sighs, one fading moment’s mirth

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: With twenty watchful, weary, tedious nights.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: If haply won, perhaps a hapless gain;

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: If lost, why then a grievous labour won;

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: However, but a folly bought with wit,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Or else a wit by folly vanquished.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: So, by your circumstance, you call me fool.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: So, by your circumstance, I fear you’ll prove.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: ’Tis love you cavil at. I am not Love.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Love is your master, for he masters you;

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: And he that is so yoked by a fool

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Methinks should not be chronicled for wise.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Yet writers say, as in the sweetest bud

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: The eating canker dwells, so eating love

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Inhabits in the finest wits of all.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: And writers say, as the most forward bud

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Is eaten by the canker ere it blow,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Even so by love the young and tender wit

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Is turned to folly, blasting in the bud,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Losing his verdure even in the prime,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: And all the fair effects of future hopes.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: But wherefore waste I time to counsel thee

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: That art a votary to fond desire?

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Once more adieu. My father at the road

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Expects my coming, there to see me shipped.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: And thither will I bring thee, Valentine.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Sweet Proteus, no. Now let us take our leave.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: To Milan let me hear from thee by letters

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Of thy success in love, and what news else

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Betideth here in absence of thy friend;

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: And I likewise will visit thee with mine.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: All happiness bechance to thee in Milan.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: As much to you at home, and so farewell.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: He after honour hunts, I after love.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: He leaves his friends to dignify them more;

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: I leave myself, my friends, and all for love.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Thou, Julia, thou hast metamorphosed me,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Made me neglect my studies, lose my time,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: War with good counsel, set the world at nought;

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Made wit with musing weak, heart sick with thought.
Enter Speed.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Sir Proteus, ’save you. Saw you my master?

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: But now he parted hence to embark for Milan.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Twenty to one, then, he is shipped already,

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: And I have played the sheep in losing him.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Indeed a sheep doth very often stray,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: An if the shepherd be a while away.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: You conclude that my master is a shepherd then, and I a sheep?

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: I do.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Why then, my horns are his horns, whether I wake or sleep.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: A silly answer, and fitting well a sheep.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: This proves me still a sheep.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: True, and thy master a shepherd.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Nay, that I can deny by a circumstance.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: It shall go hard but I’ll prove it by another.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: The shepherd seeks the sheep, and not the sheep the shepherd; but I

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: seek my master, and my master seeks not me. Therefore I am no sheep.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: The sheep for fodder follow the shepherd; the shepherd for food follows

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: not the sheep. Thou for wages followest thy master; thy master for

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: wages follows not thee. Therefore thou art a sheep.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Such another proof will make me cry “baa”.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: But dost thou hear? Gav’st thou my letter to Julia?

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Ay, sir. I, a lost mutton, gave your letter to her, a laced mutton, and

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: she, a laced mutton, gave me, a lost mutton, nothing for my labour.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Here’s too small a pasture for such store of muttons.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: If the ground be overcharged, you were best stick her.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Nay, in that you are astray; ’twere best pound you.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Nay, sir, less than a pound shall serve me for carrying your letter.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: You mistake; I mean the pound, a pinfold.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: From a pound to a pin? Fold it over and over,

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: ’Tis threefold too little for carrying a letter to your lover.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: But what said she?
[_Nods his head_.]

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Ay.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Nod—“Ay”. Why, that’s “noddy”.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: You mistook, sir. I say she did nod, and you ask me if she did nod; and

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: I say “Ay”.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: And that set together is “noddy”.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Now you have taken the pains to set it together, take it for your

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: pains.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: No, no, you shall have it for bearing the letter.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Well, I perceive I must be fain to bear with you.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Why, sir, how do you bear with me?

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Marry, sir, the letter, very orderly, having nothing but the word

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: “noddy” for my pains.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Beshrew me, but you have a quick wit.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: And yet it cannot overtake your slow purse.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Come, come, open the matter; in brief, what said she?

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Open your purse, that the money and the matter may be both at once

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: delivered.
[_Giving him a coin_.]

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Well, sir, here is for your pains. What said

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: she?

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Truly, sir, I think you’ll hardly win her.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Why? Couldst thou perceive so much from her?

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Sir, I could perceive nothing at all from her; no, not so much as a

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: ducat for delivering your letter. And being so hard to me that brought

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: your mind, I fear she’ll prove as hard to you in telling your mind.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Give her no token but stones, for she’s as hard as steel.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: What said she, nothing?

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: No, not so much as “Take this for thy pains.” To testify your bounty, I

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: thank you, you have testerned me; in requital whereof, henceforth carry

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: your letters yourself. And so, sir, I’ll commend you to my master.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Go, go, begone, to save your ship from wrack,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Which cannot perish having thee aboard,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Being destined to a drier death on shore.
[_Exit Speed._]

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: I must go send some better messenger.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: I fear my Julia would not deign my lines,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Receiving them from such a worthless post.
[_Exit._]

scenes.setting: The same. The garden of Julia’s house

lines.text: Enter Julia and Lucetta.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: But say, Lucetta, now we are alone,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Wouldst thou then counsel me to fall in love?

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: Ay, madam, so you stumble not unheedfully.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Of all the fair resort of gentlemen

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: That every day with parle encounter me,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: In thy opinion which is worthiest love?

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: Please you, repeat their names, I’ll show my mind

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: According to my shallow simple skill.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: What think’st thou of the fair Sir Eglamour?

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: As of a knight well-spoken, neat, and fine;

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: But, were I you, he never should be mine.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: What think’st thou of the rich Mercatio?

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: Well of his wealth; but of himself, so-so.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: What think’st thou of the gentle Proteus?

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: Lord, Lord, to see what folly reigns in us!

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: How now? What means this passion at his name?

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: Pardon, dear madam, ’tis a passing shame

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: That I, unworthy body as I am,

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: Should censure thus on lovely gentlemen.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Why not on Proteus, as of all the rest?

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: Then thus: of many good I think him best.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Your reason?

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: I have no other but a woman’s reason:

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: I think him so because I think him so.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: And wouldst thou have me cast my love on him?

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: Ay, if you thought your love not cast away.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Why, he of all the rest hath never moved me.

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: Yet he of all the rest I think best loves ye.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: His little speaking shows his love but small.

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: Fire that’s closest kept burns most of all.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: They do not love that do not show their love.

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: O, they love least that let men know their love.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: I would I knew his mind.

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: Peruse this paper, madam.
[_Gives her a letter._]

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: _To Julia_—Say, from whom?

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: That the contents will show.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Say, say, who gave it thee?

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: Sir Valentine’s page, and sent, I think, from Proteus.

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: He would have given it you, but I, being in the way,

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: Did in your name receive it. Pardon the fault, I pray.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Now, by my modesty, a goodly broker!

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Dare you presume to harbour wanton lines?

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: To whisper and conspire against my youth?

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Now trust me, ’tis an office of great worth,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: And you an officer fit for the place.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: There, take the paper; see it be returned,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Or else return no more into my sight.

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: To plead for love deserves more fee than hate.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Will ye be gone?

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: That you may ruminate.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: And yet I would I had o’erlooked the letter.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: It were a shame to call her back again

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: And pray her to a fault for which I chid her.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: What fool is she, that knows I am a maid

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: And would not force the letter to my view,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Since maids in modesty say “No” to that

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Which they would have the profferer construe “Ay”.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Fie, fie, how wayward is this foolish love

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: That like a testy babe will scratch the nurse

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: And presently, all humbled, kiss the rod!

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: How churlishly I chid Lucetta hence,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: When willingly I would have had her here!

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: How angerly I taught my brow to frown,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: When inward joy enforced my heart to smile!

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: My penance is to call Lucetta back

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: And ask remission for my folly past.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: What ho! Lucetta!
Enter Lucetta.

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: What would your ladyship?

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Is ’t near dinner time?

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: I would it were,

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: That you might kill your stomach on your meat

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: And not upon your maid.
[_Drops and picks up the letter._]

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: What is’t that you took up so gingerly?

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: Nothing.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Why didst thou stoop, then?

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: To take a paper up that I let fall.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: And is that paper nothing?

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: Nothing concerning me.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Then let it lie for those that it concerns.

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: Madam, it will not lie where it concerns,

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: Unless it have a false interpreter.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Some love of yours hath writ to you in rhyme.

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: That I might sing it, madam, to a tune.

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: Give me a note. Your ladyship can set—

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: As little by such toys as may be possible.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Best sing it to the tune of “Light o’ Love”.

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: It is too heavy for so light a tune.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Heavy? Belike it hath some burden then?

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: Ay, and melodious were it, would you sing it.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: And why not you?

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: I cannot reach so high.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Let’s see your song.
[_Taking the letter_.]

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: How now, minion!

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: Keep tune there still, so you will sing it out.

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: And yet methinks I do not like this tune.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: You do not?

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: No, madam, it is too sharp.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: You, minion, are too saucy.

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: Nay, now you are too flat

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: And mar the concord with too harsh a descant.

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: There wanteth but a mean to fill your song.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: The mean is drowned with your unruly bass.

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: Indeed, I bid the base for Proteus.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: This babble shall not henceforth trouble me.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Here is a coil with protestation!
[_Tears the letter_.]

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Go, get you gone, and let the papers lie.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: You would be fingering them to anger me.

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: She makes it strange, but she would be best pleased

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: To be so angered with another letter.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Nay, would I were so angered with the same!

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: O hateful hands, to tear such loving words!

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Injurious wasps, to feed on such sweet honey

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: And kill the bees that yield it with your stings!

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: I’ll kiss each several paper for amends.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Look, here is writ _kind Julia_. Unkind Julia!

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: As in revenge of thy ingratitude,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: I throw thy name against the bruising stones,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Trampling contemptuously on thy disdain.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: And here is writ _love-wounded Proteus_.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Poor wounded name, my bosom as a bed

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Shall lodge thee till thy wound be throughly healed;

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: And thus I search it with a sovereign kiss.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: But twice or thrice was _Proteus_ written down.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Be calm, good wind, blow not a word away

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Till I have found each letter in the letter

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Except mine own name. That some whirlwind bear

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Unto a ragged, fearful, hanging rock,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: And throw it thence into the raging sea.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Lo, here in one line is his name twice writ:

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: _Poor forlorn Proteus, passionate Proteus,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: To the sweet Julia._ That I’ll tear away;

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: And yet I will not, sith so prettily

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: He couples it to his complaining names.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Thus will I fold them one upon another.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Now kiss, embrace, contend, do what you will.
Enter Lucetta.

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: Madam, dinner is ready, and your father stays.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Well, let us go.

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: What, shall these papers lie like tell-tales here?

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: If you respect them, best to take them up.

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: Nay, I was taken up for laying them down.

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: Yet here they shall not lie, for catching cold.
[_Picks up pieces of the letter._]

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: I see you have a month’s mind to them.

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: Ay, madam, you may say what sights you see;

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: I see things too, although you judge I wink.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Come, come, will’t please you go?
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: The same. A room in Antonio’s house

lines.text: Enter Antonio and Pantino.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Tell me, Pantino, what sad talk was that

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Wherewith my brother held you in the cloister?

lines.speaker: PANTINO
lines.text: ’Twas of his nephew Proteus, your son.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Why, what of him?

lines.speaker: PANTINO
lines.text: He wondered that your lordship

lines.speaker: PANTINO
lines.text: Would suffer him to spend his youth at home

lines.speaker: PANTINO
lines.text: While other men, of slender reputation,

lines.speaker: PANTINO
lines.text: Put forth their sons to seek preferment out:

lines.speaker: PANTINO
lines.text: Some to the wars to try their fortune there;

lines.speaker: PANTINO
lines.text: Some to discover islands far away;

lines.speaker: PANTINO
lines.text: Some to the studious universities.

lines.speaker: PANTINO
lines.text: For any or for all these exercises

lines.speaker: PANTINO
lines.text: He said that Proteus your son was meet,

lines.speaker: PANTINO
lines.text: And did request me to importune you

lines.speaker: PANTINO
lines.text: To let him spend his time no more at home,

lines.speaker: PANTINO
lines.text: Which would be great impeachment to his age

lines.speaker: PANTINO
lines.text: In having known no travel in his youth.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Nor need’st thou much importune me to that

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Whereon this month I have been hammering.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: I have considered well his loss of time,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: And how he cannot be a perfect man,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Not being tried and tutored in the world.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Experience is by industry achieved

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: And perfected by the swift course of time.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Then tell me whither were I best to send him?

lines.speaker: PANTINO
lines.text: I think your lordship is not ignorant

lines.speaker: PANTINO
lines.text: How his companion, youthful Valentine,

lines.speaker: PANTINO
lines.text: Attends the Emperor in his royal court.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: I know it well.

lines.speaker: PANTINO
lines.text: ’Twere good, I think, your lordship sent him thither.

lines.speaker: PANTINO
lines.text: There shall he practise tilts and tournaments,

lines.speaker: PANTINO
lines.text: Hear sweet discourse, converse with noblemen,

lines.speaker: PANTINO
lines.text: And be in eye of every exercise

lines.speaker: PANTINO
lines.text: Worthy his youth and nobleness of birth.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: I like thy counsel; well hast thou advised,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: And that thou mayst perceive how well I like it,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: The execution of it shall make known.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Even with the speediest expedition

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: I will dispatch him to the Emperor’s court.

lines.speaker: PANTINO
lines.text: Tomorrow, may it please you, Don Alphonso

lines.speaker: PANTINO
lines.text: With other gentlemen of good esteem

lines.speaker: PANTINO
lines.text: Are journeying to salute the Emperor

lines.speaker: PANTINO
lines.text: And to commend their service to his will.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Good company. With them shall Proteus go.
Enter Proteus reading a letter.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: And in good time! Now will we break with him.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Sweet love, sweet lines, sweet life!

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Here is her hand, the agent of her heart;

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Here is her oath for love, her honour’s pawn.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: O, that our fathers would applaud our loves

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: To seal our happiness with their consents.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: O heavenly Julia!

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: How now? What letter are you reading there?

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: May’t please your lordship, ’tis a word or two

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Of commendations sent from Valentine,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Delivered by a friend that came from him.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Lend me the letter. Let me see what news.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: There is no news, my lord, but that he writes

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: How happily he lives, how well beloved

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: And daily graced by the Emperor,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Wishing me with him, partner of his fortune.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: And how stand you affected to his wish?

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: As one relying on your lordship’s will,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: And not depending on his friendly wish.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: My will is something sorted with his wish.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Muse not that I thus suddenly proceed,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: For what I will, I will, and there an end.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: I am resolved that thou shalt spend some time

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: With Valentinus in the Emperor’s court.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: What maintenance he from his friends receives,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Like exhibition thou shalt have from me.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Tomorrow be in readiness to go.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Excuse it not, for I am peremptory.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: My lord, I cannot be so soon provided;

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Please you deliberate a day or two.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Look what thou want’st shall be sent after thee.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: No more of stay. Tomorrow thou must go.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Come on, Pantino, you shall be employed

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: To hasten on his expedition.
[_Exeunt Antonio and Pantino._]

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Thus have I shunned the fire for fear of burning

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: And drenched me in the sea, where I am drowned.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: I feared to show my father Julia’s letter

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Lest he should take exceptions to my love,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: And with the vantage of mine own excuse

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Hath he excepted most against my love.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: O, how this spring of love resembleth

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: The uncertain glory of an April day,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Which now shows all the beauty of the sun,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: And by an by a cloud takes all away.
Enter Pantino.

lines.speaker: PANTINO
lines.text: Sir Proteus, your father calls for you.

lines.speaker: PANTINO
lines.text: He is in haste. Therefore, I pray you, go.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Why, this it is: my heart accords thereto,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: And yet a thousand times it answers “No”.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: Milan. A room in the Duke’s palace

lines.text: Enter Valentine and Speed.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Sir, your glove.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Not mine. My gloves are on.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Why, then, this may be yours, for this is but one.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Ha? Let me see. Ay, give it me, it’s mine.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Sweet ornament that decks a thing divine!

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Ah, Silvia, Silvia!
[_Calling_.]

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Madam Silvia! Madam Silvia!

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: How now, sirrah?

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: She is not within hearing, sir.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Why, sir, who bade you call her?

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Your worship, sir, or else I mistook.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Well, you’ll still be too forward.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: And yet I was last chidden for being too slow.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Go to, sir. Tell me, do you know Madam Silvia?

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: She that your worship loves?

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Why, how know you that I am in love?

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Marry, by these special marks: first, you have learned, like Sir

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Proteus, to wreathe your arms like a malcontent; to relish a love-song,

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: like a robin redbreast; to walk alone, like one that had the

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: pestilence; to sigh, like a schoolboy that had lost his ABC; to weep,

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: like a young wench that had buried her grandam; to fast, like one that

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: takes diet; to watch, like one that fears robbing; to speak puling,

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: like a beggar at Hallowmas. You were wont, when you laughed, to crow

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: like a cock; when you walked, to walk like one of the lions; when you

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: fasted, it was presently after dinner; when you looked sadly, it was

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: for want of money. And now you are metamorphosed with a mistress, that,

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: when I look on you, I can hardly think you my master.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Are all these things perceived in me?

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: They are all perceived without ye.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Without me? They cannot.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Without you? Nay, that’s certain, for without you were so simple, none

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: else would. But you are so without these follies, that these follies

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: are within you, and shine through you like the water in an urinal, that

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: not an eye that sees you but is a physician to comment on your malady.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: But tell me, dost thou know my lady Silvia?

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: She that you gaze on so as she sits at supper?

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Hast thou observed that? Even she I mean.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Why, sir, I know her not.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Dost thou know her by my gazing on her, and yet know’st her not?

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Is she not hard-favoured, sir?

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Not so fair, boy, as well-favoured.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Sir, I know that well enough.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: What dost thou know?

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: That she is not so fair as, of you, well-favoured.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: I mean that her beauty is exquisite but her favour infinite.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: That’s because the one is painted, and the other out of all count.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: How painted? And how out of count?

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Marry, sir, so painted to make her fair, that no man counts of her

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: beauty.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: How esteem’st thou me? I account of her beauty.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: You never saw her since she was deformed.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: How long hath she been deformed?

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Ever since you loved her.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: I have loved her ever since I saw her, and still I see her beautiful.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: If you love her, you cannot see her.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Why?

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Because Love is blind. O, that you had mine eyes, or your own eyes had

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: the lights they were wont to have when you chid at Sir Proteus for

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: going ungartered!

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: What should I see then?

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Your own present folly and her passing deformity; for he, being in

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: love, could not see to garter his hose; and you, being in love, cannot

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: see to put on your hose.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Belike, boy, then you are in love, for last morning you could not see

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: to wipe my shoes.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: True, sir, I was in love with my bed. I thank you, you swinged me for

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: my love, which makes me the bolder to chide you for yours.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: In conclusion, I stand affected to her.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: I would you were set, so your affection would cease.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Last night she enjoined me to write some lines to one she loves.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: And have you?

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: I have.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Are they not lamely writ?

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: No, boy, but as well as I can do them.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Peace, here she comes.
Enter Silvia.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: O excellent motion! O exceeding puppet!

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Now will he interpret to her.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Madam and mistress, a thousand good-morrows.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: O, give ye good e’en! Here’s a million of manners.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Sir Valentine and servant, to you two thousand.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: He should give her interest, and she gives it him.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: As you enjoined me, I have writ your letter

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Unto the secret nameless friend of yours,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Which I was much unwilling to proceed in

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: But for my duty to your ladyship.
[_Gives her a letter._]

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: I thank you, gentle servant, ’tis very clerkly done.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Now trust me, madam, it came hardly off,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: For, being ignorant to whom it goes,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: I writ at random, very doubtfully.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Perchance you think too much of so much pains?

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: No, madam; so it stead you, I will write,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Please you command, a thousand times as much.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: And yet—

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: A pretty period. Well, I guess the sequel;

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: And yet I will not name it. And yet I care not.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: And yet take this again.
[_Offers him the letter._]

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: And yet I thank you,

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Meaning henceforth to trouble you no more.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: And yet you will; and yet another “yet”.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: What means your ladyship? Do you not like it?

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Yes, yes, the lines are very quaintly writ,

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: But, since unwillingly, take them again.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Nay, take them.
[_Offers the letter again._]

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Madam, they are for you.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Ay, ay, you writ them, sir, at my request,

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: But I will none of them. They are for you.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: I would have had them writ more movingly.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Please you, I’ll write your ladyship another.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: And when it’s writ, for my sake read it over,

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: And if it please you, so; if not, why, so.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: If it please me, madam? What then?

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Why, if it please you, take it for your labour.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: And so good morrow, servant.
[_Exit._]
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: O jest unseen, inscrutable, invisible,

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: As a nose on a man’s face, or a weathercock on a steeple!

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: My master sues to her, and she hath taught her suitor,

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: He being her pupil, to become her tutor.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: O excellent device! Was there ever heard a better?

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: That my master, being scribe, to himself should write the letter?

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: How now, sir? What are you reasoning with yourself?

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Nay, I was rhyming. ’Tis you that have the reason.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: To do what?

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: To be a spokesman from Madam Silvia.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: To whom?

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: To yourself. Why, she woos you by a figure.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: What figure?

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: By a letter, I should say.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Why, she hath not writ to me.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: What need she, when she hath made you write to yourself? Why, do you

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: not perceive the jest?

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: No, believe me.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: No believing you indeed, sir. But did you perceive her earnest?

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: She gave me none, except an angry word.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Why, she hath given you a letter.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: That’s the letter I writ to her friend.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: And that letter hath she delivered, and there an end.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: I would it were no worse.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: I’ll warrant you, ’tis as well.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: For often have you writ to her, and she, in modesty

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Or else for want of idle time, could not again reply,

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Or fearing else some messenger that might her mind discover,

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Herself hath taught her love himself to write unto her lover.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: All this I speak in print, for in print I found it. Why muse you, sir?

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: ’Tis dinner time.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: I have dined.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Ay, but hearken, sir, though the chameleon Love can feed on the air, I

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: am one that am nourished by my victuals, and would fain have meat. O,

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: be not like your mistress! Be moved, be moved.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: Verona. A room in Julia’s house

lines.text: Enter Proteus and Julia.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Have patience, gentle Julia.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: I must, where is no remedy.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: When possibly I can, I will return.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: If you turn not, you will return the sooner.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Keep this remembrance for thy Julia’s sake.
[_Gives him a ring._]

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Why, then we’ll make exchange. Here, take you this.
[_Gives her a ring._]

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: And seal the bargain with a holy kiss.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Here is my hand for my true constancy.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: And when that hour o’erslips me in the day

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Wherein I sigh not, Julia, for thy sake,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: The next ensuing hour some foul mischance

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Torment me for my love’s forgetfulness.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: My father stays my coming; answer not.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: The tide is now—nay, not thy tide of tears,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: That tide will stay me longer than I should.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Julia, farewell.
[_Exit Julia._]

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: What, gone without a word?

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Ay, so true love should do. It cannot speak,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: For truth hath better deeds than words to grace it.
Enter Pantino.

lines.speaker: PANTINO
lines.text: Sir Proteus, you are stayed for.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Go, I come, I come.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Alas, this parting strikes poor lovers dumb.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: The same. A street

lines.text: Enter Lance with his dog Crab.

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: Nay, ’twill be this hour ere I have done weeping; all the kind of the

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: Lances have this very fault. I have received my proportion, like the

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: prodigious son, and am going with Sir Proteus to the Imperial’s court.

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: I think Crab my dog be the sourest-natured dog that lives: my mother

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: weeping, my father wailing, my sister crying, our maid howling, our cat

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: wringing her hands, and all our house in a great perplexity, yet did

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: not this cruel-hearted cur shed one tear. He is a stone, a very

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: pebblestone, and has no more pity in him than a dog. A Jew would have

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: wept to have seen our parting. Why, my grandam, having no eyes, look

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: you, wept herself blind at my parting. Nay, I’ll show you the manner of

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: it. This shoe is my father. No, this left shoe is my father; no, no,

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: this left shoe is my mother. Nay, that cannot be so neither. Yes, it is

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: so, it is so; it hath the worser sole. This shoe with the hole in it is

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: my mother, and this my father. A vengeance on ’t, there ’tis. Now, sir,

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: this staff is my sister, for, look you, she is as white as a lily and

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: as small as a wand. This hat is Nan, our maid. I am the dog. No, the

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: dog is himself, and I am the dog. O, the dog is me, and I am myself.

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: Ay, so, so. Now come I to my father: “Father, your blessing.” Now

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: should not the shoe speak a word for weeping. Now should I kiss my

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: father. Well, he weeps on. Now come I to my mother. O, that she could

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: speak now like a wood woman! Well, I kiss her. Why there ’tis; here’s

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: my mother’s breath up and down. Now come I to my sister. Mark the moan

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: she makes. Now the dog all this while sheds not a tear nor speaks a

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: word; but see how I lay the dust with my tears.
Enter Pantino.

lines.speaker: PANTINO
lines.text: Lance, away, away! Aboard! Thy master is shipped, and thou art to post

lines.speaker: PANTINO
lines.text: after with oars. What’s the matter? Why weep’st thou, man? Away, ass.

lines.speaker: PANTINO
lines.text: You’ll lose the tide if you tarry any longer.

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: It is no matter if the tied were lost, for it is the unkindest tied

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: that ever any man tied.

lines.speaker: PANTINO
lines.text: What’s the unkindest tide?

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: Why, he that’s tied here, Crab, my dog.

lines.speaker: PANTINO
lines.text: Tut, man, I mean thou’lt lose the flood, and, in losing the flood, lose

lines.speaker: PANTINO
lines.text: thy voyage, and, in losing thy voyage, lose thy master, and, in losing

lines.speaker: PANTINO
lines.text: thy master, lose thy service, and, in losing thy service—why dost thou

lines.speaker: PANTINO
lines.text: stop my mouth?

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: For fear thou shouldst lose thy tongue.

lines.speaker: PANTINO
lines.text: Where should I lose my tongue?

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: In thy tale.

lines.speaker: PANTINO
lines.text: In thy tail!

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: Lose the tide, and the voyage, and the master, and the service, and the

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: tied? Why, man, if the river were dry, I am able to fill it with my

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: tears; if the wind were down, I could drive the boat with my sighs.

lines.speaker: PANTINO
lines.text: Come, come away, man. I was sent to call thee.

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: Sir, call me what thou dar’st.

lines.speaker: PANTINO
lines.text: Will thou go?

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: Well, I will go.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: Milan. A room in the Duke’s palace

lines.text: Enter Valentine, Silvia, Thurio and Speed.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Servant!

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Mistress?

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Master, Sir Thurio frowns on you.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Ay, boy, it’s for love.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Not of you.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Of my mistress, then.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: ’Twere good you knocked him.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Servant, you are sad.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Indeed, madam, I seem so.

lines.speaker: THURIO
lines.text: Seem you that you are not?

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Haply I do.

lines.speaker: THURIO
lines.text: So do counterfeits.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: So do you.

lines.speaker: THURIO
lines.text: What seem I that I am not?

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Wise.

lines.speaker: THURIO
lines.text: What instance of the contrary?

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Your folly.

lines.speaker: THURIO
lines.text: And how quote you my folly?

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: I quote it in your jerkin.

lines.speaker: THURIO
lines.text: My jerkin is a doublet.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Well, then, I’ll double your folly.

lines.speaker: THURIO
lines.text: How!

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: What, angry, Sir Thurio? Do you change colour?

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Give him leave, madam, he is a kind of chameleon.

lines.speaker: THURIO
lines.text: That hath more mind to feed on your blood than live in your air.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: You have said, sir.

lines.speaker: THURIO
lines.text: Ay, sir, and done too, for this time.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: I know it well, sir. You always end ere you begin.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: A fine volley of words, gentlemen, and quickly shot off.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: ’Tis indeed, madam, we thank the giver.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Who is that, servant?

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Yourself, sweet lady, for you gave the fire. Sir Thurio borrows his wit

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: from your ladyship’s looks, and spends what he borrows kindly in your

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: company.

lines.speaker: THURIO
lines.text: Sir, if you spend word for word with me, I shall make your wit

lines.speaker: THURIO
lines.text: bankrupt.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: I know it well, sir. You have an exchequer of words and, I think, no

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: other treasure to give your followers, for it appears by their bare

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: liveries that they live by your bare words.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: No more, gentlemen, no more. Here comes my father.
Enter Duke.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Now, daughter Silvia, you are hard beset.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Sir Valentine, your father is in good health.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: What say you to a letter from your friends

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Of much good news?

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: My lord, I will be thankful

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: To any happy messenger from thence.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Know ye Don Antonio, your countryman?

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Ay, my good lord, I know the gentleman

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: To be of worth and worthy estimation,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: And not without desert so well reputed.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Hath he not a son?

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Ay, my good lord, a son that well deserves

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: The honour and regard of such a father.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: You know him well?

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: I knew him as myself, for from our infancy

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: We have conversed and spent our hours together.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: And though myself have been an idle truant,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Omitting the sweet benefit of time

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: To clothe mine age with angel-like perfection,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Yet hath Sir Proteus, for that’s his name,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Made use and fair advantage of his days:

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: His years but young, but his experience old;

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: His head unmellowed, but his judgement ripe;

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: And in a word, for far behind his worth

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Comes all the praises that I now bestow,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: He is complete in feature and in mind,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: With all good grace to grace a gentleman.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Beshrew me, sir, but if he make this good,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: He is as worthy for an empress’ love

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: As meet to be an emperor’s counsellor.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Well, sir, this gentleman is come to me

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: With commendation from great potentates,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: And here he means to spend his time awhile.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: I think ’tis no unwelcome news to you.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Should I have wished a thing, it had been he.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Welcome him then according to his worth.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Silvia, I speak to you, and you, Sir Thurio.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: For Valentine, I need not cite him to it.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: I will send him hither to you presently.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: This is the gentleman I told your ladyship

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Had come along with me but that his mistresss

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Did hold his eyes locked in her crystal looks.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Belike that now she hath enfranchised them

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Upon some other pawn for fealty.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Nay, sure, I think she holds them prisoners still.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Nay, then, he should be blind, and being blind

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: How could he see his way to seek out you?

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Why, lady, Love hath twenty pair of eyes.

lines.speaker: THURIO
lines.text: They say that Love hath not an eye at all.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: To see such lovers, Thurio, as yourself.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Upon a homely object, Love can wink.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Have done, have done. Here comes the gentleman.
Enter Proteus.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Welcome, dear Proteus! Mistress, I beseech you

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Confirm his welcome with some special favour.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: His worth is warrant for his welcome hither,

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: If this be he you oft have wished to hear from.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Mistress, it is. Sweet lady, entertain him

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: To be my fellow-servant to your ladyship.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Too low a mistress for so high a servant.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Not so, sweet lady, but too mean a servant

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: To have a look of such a worthy mistress.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Leave off discourse of disability.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Sweet lady, entertain him for your servant.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: My duty will I boast of, nothing else.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: And duty never yet did want his meed.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Servant, you are welcome to a worthless mistress.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: I’ll die on him that says so but yourself.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: That you are welcome?

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: That you are worthless.
Enter Servant.

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: Madam, my lord your father would speak with you.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: I wait upon his pleasure.
[_Exit Servant._]

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Come, Sir Thurio,

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Go with me.—Once more, new servant, welcome.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: I’ll leave you to confer of home affairs;

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: When you have done, we look to hear from you.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: We’ll both attend upon your ladyship.
[_Exeunt Silvia and Thurio._]

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Now, tell me, how do all from whence you came?

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Your friends are well and have them much commended.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: And how do yours?

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: I left them all in health.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: How does your lady? And how thrives your love?

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: My tales of love were wont to weary you;

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: I know you joy not in a love-discourse.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Ay, Proteus, but that life is altered now.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: I have done penance for contemning Love,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Whose high imperious thoughts have punished me

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: With bitter fasts, with penitential groans,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: With nightly tears, and daily heart-sore sighs;

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: For in revenge of my contempt of love,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Love hath chased sleep from my enthralled eyes

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: And made them watchers of mine own heart’s sorrow.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: O gentle Proteus, Love’s a mighty lord,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: And hath so humbled me as I confess

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: There is no woe to his correction,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Nor to his service no such joy on earth.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Now, no discourse, except it be of love;

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Now can I break my fast, dine, sup, and sleep

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Upon the very naked name of love.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Enough; I read your fortune in your eye.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Was this the idol that you worship so?

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Even she; and is she not a heavenly saint?

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: No, but she is an earthly paragon.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Call her divine.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: I will not flatter her.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: O, flatter me, for love delights in praises.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: When I was sick, you gave me bitter pills,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: And I must minister the like to you.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Then speak the truth by her; if not divine,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Yet let her be a principality,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Sovereign to all the creatures on the earth.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Except my mistress.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Sweet, except not any,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Except thou wilt except against my love.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Have I not reason to prefer mine own?

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: And I will help thee to prefer her too:

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: She shall be dignified with this high honour,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: To bear my lady’s train, lest the base earth

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Should from her vesture chance to steal a kiss,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: And, of so great a favour growing proud,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Disdain to root the summer-swelling flower

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: And make rough winter everlastingly.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Why, Valentine, what braggartism is this?

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Pardon me, Proteus, all I can is nothing

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: To her, whose worth makes other worthies nothing;

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: She is alone.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Then let her alone.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Not for the world! Why, man, she is mine own,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: And I as rich in having such a jewel

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: As twenty seas, if all their sand were pearl,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: The water nectar, and the rocks pure gold.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Forgive me that I do not dream on thee,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Because thou seest me dote upon my love.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: My foolish rival, that her father likes

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Only for his possessions are so huge,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Is gone with her along, and I must after,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: For love, thou know’st, is full of jealousy.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: But she loves you?

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Ay, and we are betrothed; nay more, our marriage hour,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: With all the cunning manner of our flight,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Determined of: how I must climb her window,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: The ladder made of cords, and all the means

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Plotted and ’greed on for my happiness.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Good Proteus, go with me to my chamber,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: In these affairs to aid me with thy counsel.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Go on before; I shall enquire you forth.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: I must unto the road to disembark

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Some necessaries that I needs must use,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: And then I’ll presently attend you.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Will you make haste?

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: I will.
[_Exit Valentine._]

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Even as one heat another heat expels,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Or as one nail by strength drives out another,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: So the remembrance of my former love

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Is by a newer object quite forgotten.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Is it mine eye, or Valentine’s praise,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Her true perfection, or my false transgression,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: That makes me reasonless to reason thus?

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: She is fair; and so is Julia that I love—

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: That I did love, for now my love is thawed,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Which like a waxen image ’gainst a fire

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Bears no impression of the thing it was.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Methinks my zeal to Valentine is cold,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: And that I love him not as I was wont.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: O, but I love his lady too too much,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: And that’s the reason I love him so little.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: How shall I dote on her with more advice

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: That thus without advice begin to love her?

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: ’Tis but her picture I have yet beheld,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: And that hath dazzled my reason’s light;

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: But when I look on her perfections,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: There is no reason but I shall be blind.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: If I can check my erring love, I will;

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: If not, to compass her I’ll use my skill.
[_Exit._]

scenes.setting: The same. A street

lines.text: Enter Speed and Lance with his dog Crab.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Lance, by mine honesty, welcome to Milan!

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: Forswear not thyself, sweet youth, for I am not welcome. I reckon this

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: always, that a man is never undone till he be hanged, nor never welcome

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: to a place till some certain shot be paid and the hostess say

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: “Welcome”.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Come on, you madcap. I’ll to the alehouse with you presently, where,

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: for one shot of five pence, thou shalt have five thousand welcomes.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: But, sirrah, how did thy master part with Madam Julia?

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: Marry, after they closed in earnest, they parted very fairly in jest.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: But shall she marry him?

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: How then? Shall he marry her?

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: No, neither.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: What, are they broken?

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: No, they are both as whole as a fish.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Why then, how stands the matter with them?

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: Marry, thus: when it stands well with him, it stands well with her.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: What an ass art thou! I understand thee not.

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: What a block art thou that thou canst not! My staff understands me.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: What thou sayst?

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: Ay, and what I do too. Look thee, I’ll but lean, and my staff

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: understands me.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: It stands under thee indeed.

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: Why, stand-under and under-stand is all one.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: But tell me true, will’t be a match?

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: Ask my dog. If he say “Ay”, it will; if he say “No”, it will; if he

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: shake his tail and say nothing, it will.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: The conclusion is, then, that it will.

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: Thou shalt never get such a secret from me but by a parable.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: ’Tis well that I get it so. But, Lance, how sayst thou that my master

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: is become a notable lover?

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: I never knew him otherwise.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Than how?

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: A notable lubber, as thou reportest him to be.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Why, thou whoreson ass, thou mistak’st me.

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: Why, fool, I meant not thee, I meant thy master.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: I tell thee, my master is become a hot lover.

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: Why, I tell thee, I care not though he burn himself in love. If thou

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: wilt, go with me to the alehouse; if not, thou art an Hebrew, a Jew,

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: and not worth the name of a Christian.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Why?

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: Because thou hast not so much charity in thee as to go to the ale with

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: a Christian. Wilt thou go?

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: At thy service.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: The same. The Duke’s palace

lines.text: Enter Proteus alone.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: To leave my Julia, shall I be forsworn;

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: To love fair Silvia, shall I be forsworn;

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: To wrong my friend, I shall be much forsworn.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: And e’en that power which gave me first my oath

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Provokes me to this threefold perjury.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Love bade me swear, and Love bids me forswear.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: O sweet-suggesting Love, if thou hast sinned,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Teach me, thy tempted subject, to excuse it.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: At first I did adore a twinkling star,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: But now I worship a celestial sun.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Unheedful vows may heedfully be broken,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: And he wants wit that wants resolved will

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: To learn his wit t’ exchange the bad for better.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Fie, fie, unreverend tongue, to call her bad

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Whose sovereignty so oft thou hast preferred

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: With twenty thousand soul-confirming oaths.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: I cannot leave to love, and yet I do;

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: But there I leave to love where I should love.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Julia I lose, and Valentine I lose;

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: If I keep them, I needs must lose myself;

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: If I lose them, thus find I by their loss,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: For Valentine, myself; for Julia, Silvia.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: I to myself am dearer than a friend,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: For love is still most precious in itself,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: And Silvia—witness heaven that made her fair—

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Shows Julia but a swarthy Ethiope.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: I will forget that Julia is alive,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Remembering that my love to her is dead;

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: And Valentine I’ll hold an enemy,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Aiming at Silvia as a sweeter friend.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: I cannot now prove constant to myself

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Without some treachery used to Valentine.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: This night he meaneth with a corded ladder

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: To climb celestial Silvia’s chamber window,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Myself in counsel, his competitor.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Now presently I’ll give her father notice

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Of their disguising and pretended flight,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Who, all enraged, will banish Valentine,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: For Thurio he intends shall wed his daughter.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: But Valentine being gone, I’ll quickly cross

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: By some sly trick blunt Thurio’s dull proceeding.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Love, lend me wings to make my purpose swift,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: As thou hast lent me wit to plot this drift.
[_Exit._]

scenes.setting: Verona. A room in Julia’s house

lines.text: Enter Julia and Lucetta.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Counsel, Lucetta; gentle girl, assist me,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: And ev’n in kind love I do conjure thee,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Who art the table wherein all my thoughts

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Are visibly charactered and engraved,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: To lesson me and tell me some good mean

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: How with my honour I may undertake

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: A journey to my loving Proteus.

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: Alas, the way is wearisome and long.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: A true-devoted pilgrim is not weary

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: To measure kingdoms with his feeble steps;

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Much less shall she that hath Love’s wings to fly,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: And when the flight is made to one so dear,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Of such divine perfection, as Sir Proteus.

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: Better forbear till Proteus make return.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: O, know’st thou not his looks are my soul’s food?

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Pity the dearth that I have pined in

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: By longing for that food so long a time.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Didst thou but know the inly touch of love

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Thou wouldst as soon go kindle fire with snow

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: As seek to quench the fire of love with words.

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: I do not seek to quench your love’s hot fire,

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: But qualify the fire’s extreme rage,

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: Lest it should burn above the bounds of reason.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: The more thou damm’st it up, the more it burns.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: The current that with gentle murmur glides,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Thou know’st, being stopped, impatiently doth rage;

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: But when his fair course is not hindered,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: He makes sweet music with th’ enamelled stones,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Giving a gentle kiss to every sedge

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: He overtaketh in his pilgrimage;

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: And so by many winding nooks he strays

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: With willing sport to the wild ocean.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Then let me go and hinder not my course.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: I’ll be as patient as a gentle stream

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: And make a pastime of each weary step

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Till the last step have brought me to my love,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: And there I’ll rest as after much turmoil

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: A blessed soul doth in Elysium.

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: But in what habit will you go along?

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Not like a woman, for I would prevent

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: The loose encounters of lascivious men.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Gentle Lucetta, fit me with such weeds

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: As may beseem some well-reputed page.

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: Why then, your ladyship must cut your hair.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: No, girl, I’ll knit it up in silken strings

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: With twenty odd-conceited true-love knots.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: To be fantastic may become a youth

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Of greater time than I shall show to be.

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: What fashion, madam, shall I make your breeches?

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: That fits as well as “Tell me, good my lord,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: What compass will you wear your farthingale?”

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Why e’en what fashion thou best likes, Lucetta.

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: You must needs have them with a codpiece, madam.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Out, out, Lucetta, that will be ill-favoured.

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: A round hose, madam, now’s not worth a pin

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: Unless you have a codpiece to stick pins on.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Lucetta, as thou lov’st me, let me have

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: What thou think’st meet and is most mannerly.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: But tell me, wench, how will the world repute me

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: For undertaking so unstaid a journey?

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: I fear me it will make me scandalized.

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: If you think so, then stay at home and go not.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Nay, that I will not.

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: Then never dream on infamy, but go.

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: If Proteus like your journey when you come,

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: No matter who’s displeased when you are gone.

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: I fear me he will scarce be pleased withal.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: That is the least, Lucetta, of my fear.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: A thousand oaths, an ocean of his tears,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: And instances of infinite of love,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Warrant me welcome to my Proteus.

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: All these are servants to deceitful men.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Base men that use them to so base effect!

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: But truer stars did govern Proteus’ birth.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: His words are bonds, his oaths are oracles,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: His love sincere, his thoughts immaculate,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: His tears pure messengers sent from his heart,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: His heart as far from fraud as heaven from earth.

lines.speaker: LUCETTA
lines.text: Pray heav’n he prove so when you come to him.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Now, as thou lov’st me, do him not that wrong

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: To bear a hard opinion of his truth.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Only deserve my love by loving him.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: And presently go with me to my chamber

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: To take a note of what I stand in need of

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: To furnish me upon my longing journey.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: All that is mine I leave at thy dispose,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: My goods, my lands, my reputation;

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Only, in lieu thereof, dispatch me hence.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Come, answer not, but to it presently.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: I am impatient of my tarriance.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: Milan. An anteroom in the Duke’s palace

lines.text: Enter Duke, Thurio and Proteus.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Sir Thurio, give us leave, I pray, awhile;

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: We have some secrets to confer about.
[_Exit Thurio._]

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Now tell me, Proteus, what’s your will with me?

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: My gracious lord, that which I would discover

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: The law of friendship bids me to conceal,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: But when I call to mind your gracious favours

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Done to me, undeserving as I am,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: My duty pricks me on to utter that

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Which else no worldly good should draw from me.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Know, worthy prince, Sir Valentine my friend

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: This night intends to steal away your daughter;

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Myself am one made privy to the plot.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: I know you have determined to bestow her

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: On Thurio, whom your gentle daughter hates,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: And should she thus be stol’n away from you,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: It would be much vexation to your age.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Thus, for my duty’s sake, I rather chose

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: To cross my friend in his intended drift

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Than, by concealing it, heap on your head

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: A pack of sorrows which would press you down,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Being unprevented, to your timeless grave.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Proteus, I thank thee for thine honest care,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Which to requite command me while I live.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: This love of theirs myself have often seen,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Haply when they have judged me fast asleep,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: And oftentimes have purposed to forbid

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Sir Valentine her company and my court.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: But fearing lest my jealous aim might err

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: And so, unworthily, disgrace the man—

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: A rashness that I ever yet have shunned—

lines.speaker: DUKE
