lines.text: I gave him gentle looks, thereby to find

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: That which thyself hast now disclosed to me.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: And that thou mayst perceive my fear of this,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Knowing that tender youth is soon suggested,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: I nightly lodge her in an upper tower,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: The key whereof myself have ever kept;

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: And thence she cannot be conveyed away.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Know, noble lord, they have devised a mean

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: How he her chamber-window will ascend

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: And with a corded ladder fetch her down;

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: For which the youthful lover now is gone,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: And this way comes he with it presently,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Where, if it please you, you may intercept him.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: But, good my lord, do it so cunningly

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: That my discovery be not aimed at;

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: For love of you, not hate unto my friend,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Hath made me publisher of this pretence.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Upon mine honour, he shall never know

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: That I had any light from thee of this.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Adieu, my lord, Sir Valentine is coming.
[_Exit._]
Enter Valentine.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Sir Valentine, whither away so fast?

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Please it your Grace, there is a messenger

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: That stays to bear my letters to my friends,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: And I am going to deliver them.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Be they of much import?

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: The tenor of them doth but signify

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: My health and happy being at your court.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Nay then, no matter. Stay with me awhile;

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: I am to break with thee of some affairs

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: That touch me near, wherein thou must be secret.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: ’Tis not unknown to thee that I have sought

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: To match my friend Sir Thurio to my daughter.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: I know it well, my lord, and sure the match

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Were rich and honourable. Besides, the gentleman

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Is full of virtue, bounty, worth, and qualities

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Beseeming such a wife as your fair daughter.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Cannot your grace win her to fancy him?

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: No, trust me, she is peevish, sullen, froward,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Proud, disobedient, stubborn, lacking duty,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Neither regarding that she is my child

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Nor fearing me as if I were her father;

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: And, may I say to thee, this pride of hers,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Upon advice, hath drawn my love from her,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: And where I thought the remnant of mine age

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Should have been cherished by her childlike duty,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: I now am full resolved to take a wife

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: And turn her out to who will take her in.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Then let her beauty be her wedding dower,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: For me and my possessions she esteems not.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: What would your Grace have me to do in this?

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: There is a lady of Verona here

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Whom I affect; but she is nice, and coy,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: And nought esteems my aged eloquence.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Now therefore would I have thee to my tutor—

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: For long agone I have forgot to court;

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Besides, the fashion of the time is changed—

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: How and which way I may bestow myself

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: To be regarded in her sun-bright eye.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Win her with gifts if she respect not words;

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Dumb jewels often in their silent kind

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: More than quick words do move a woman’s mind.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: But she did scorn a present that I sent her.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: A woman sometime scorns what best contents her.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Send her another; never give her o’er,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: For scorn at first makes after-love the more.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: If she do frown, ’tis not in hate of you,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: But rather to beget more love in you.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: If she do chide, ’tis not to have you gone,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Forwhy the fools are mad if left alone.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Take no repulse, whatever she doth say;

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: For “Get you gone” she doth not mean “Away!”

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Flatter and praise, commend, extol their graces;

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Though ne’er so black, say they have angels’ faces.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: That man that hath a tongue, I say, is no man

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: If with his tongue he cannot win a woman.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: But she I mean is promised by her friends

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Unto a youthful gentleman of worth,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: And kept severely from resort of men,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: That no man hath access by day to her.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Why then, I would resort to her by night.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Ay, but the doors be locked and keys kept safe,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: That no man hath recourse to her by night.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: What lets but one may enter at her window?

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Her chamber is aloft, far from the ground,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: And built so shelving that one cannot climb it

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Without apparent hazard of his life.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Why, then a ladder quaintly made of cords

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: To cast up with a pair of anchoring hooks,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Would serve to scale another Hero’s tower,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: So bold Leander would adventure it.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Now, as thou art a gentleman of blood,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Advise me where I may have such a ladder.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: When would you use it? Pray, sir, tell me that.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: This very night; for Love is like a child

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: That longs for everything that he can come by.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: By seven o’clock I’ll get you such a ladder.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: But, hark thee: I will go to her alone;

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: How shall I best convey the ladder thither?

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: It will be light, my lord, that you may bear it

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Under a cloak that is of any length.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: A cloak as long as thine will serve the turn?

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Ay, my good lord.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Then let me see thy cloak;

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: I’ll get me one of such another length.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Why, any cloak will serve the turn, my lord.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: How shall I fashion me to wear a cloak?

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: I pray thee, let me feel thy cloak upon me.
[_Takes Valentine’s cloak and finds a letter and a rope ladder concealed under it._]

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: What letter is this same? What’s here?—_To Silvia?_

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: And here an engine fit for my proceeding.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: I’ll be so bold to break the seal for once.
[_Reads_.]

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: _My thoughts do harbour with my Silvia nightly,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: And slaves they are to me that send them flying.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: O, could their master come and go as lightly,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Himself would lodge where, senseless, they are lying.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: My herald thoughts in thy pure bosom rest them,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: While I, their king, that thither them importune,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Do curse the grace that with such grace hath blest them,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Because myself do want my servants’ fortune.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: I curse myself, for they are sent by me,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: That they should harbour where their lord should be._

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: What’s here?
[_Reads_.]

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: _Silvia, this night I will enfranchise thee._

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: ’Tis so; and here’s the ladder for the purpose.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Why, Phaëthon—for thou art Merops’ son—

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Wilt thou aspire to guide the heavenly car,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: And with thy daring folly burn the world?

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Wilt thou reach stars because they shine on thee?

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Go, base intruder, overweening slave,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Bestow thy fawning smiles on equal mates,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: And think my patience, more than thy desert,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Is privilege for thy departure hence.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Thank me for this more than for all the favours

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Which, all too much, I have bestowed on thee.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: But if thou linger in my territories

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Longer than swiftest expedition

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Will give thee time to leave our royal court,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: By heaven, my wrath shall far exceed the love

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: I ever bore my daughter or thyself.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Begone, I will not hear thy vain excuse,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: But, as thou lov’st thy life, make speed from hence.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: And why not death, rather than living torment?

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: To die is to be banished from myself,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: And Silvia is myself; banished from her

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Is self from self—a deadly banishment.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: What light is light, if Silvia be not seen?

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: What joy is joy, if Silvia be not by?

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Unless it be to think that she is by

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: And feed upon the shadow of perfection.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Except I be by Silvia in the night,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: There is no music in the nightingale.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Unless I look on Silvia in the day,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: There is no day for me to look upon.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: She is my essence, and I leave to be

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: If I be not by her fair influence

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Fostered, illumined, cherished, kept alive.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: I fly not death, to fly his deadly doom:

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Tarry I here, I but attend on death,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: But fly I hence, I fly away from life.
Enter Proteus and Lance.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Run, boy, run, run, seek him out.

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: So-ho, so-ho!

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: What seest thou?

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: Him we go to find. There’s not a hair on ’s head but ’tis a Valentine.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Valentine?

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Who then? His spirit?

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Neither.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: What then?

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Nothing.

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: Can nothing speak? Master, shall I strike?

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Who wouldst thou strike?

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: Nothing.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Villain, forbear.

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: Why, sir, I’ll strike nothing. I pray you—

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Sirrah, I say, forbear.—Friend Valentine, a word.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: My ears are stopped and cannot hear good news,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: So much of bad already hath possessed them.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Then in dumb silence will I bury mine,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: For they are harsh, untuneable, and bad.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Is Silvia dead?

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: No, Valentine.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: No Valentine indeed for sacred Silvia.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Hath she forsworn me?

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: No, Valentine.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: No Valentine, if Silvia have forsworn me.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: What is your news?

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: Sir, there is a proclamation that you are vanished.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: That thou art banished—O, that’s the news—

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: From hence, from Silvia, and from me thy friend.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: O, I have fed upon this woe already,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: And now excess of it will make me surfeit.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Doth Silvia know that I am banished?

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Ay, ay; and she hath offered to the doom—

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Which unreversed stands in effectual force—

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: A sea of melting pearl, which some call tears;

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Those at her father’s churlish feet she tendered,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: With them, upon her knees, her humble self,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Wringing her hands, whose whiteness so became them

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: As if but now they waxed pale for woe.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: But neither bended knees, pure hands held up,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Sad sighs, deep groans, nor silver-shedding tears

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Could penetrate her uncompassionate sire;

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: But Valentine, if he be ta’en, must die.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Besides, her intercession chafed him so,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: When she for thy repeal was suppliant,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: That to close prison he commanded her,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: With many bitter threats of biding there.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: No more, unless the next word that thou speak’st

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Have some malignant power upon my life.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: If so, I pray thee breathe it in mine ear,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: As ending anthem of my endless dolour.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Cease to lament for that thou canst not help,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: And study help for that which thou lament’st.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Time is the nurse and breeder of all good.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Here if thou stay, thou canst not see thy love;

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Besides, thy staying will abridge thy life.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Hope is a lover’s staff; walk hence with that

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: And manage it against despairing thoughts.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Thy letters may be here, though thou art hence,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Which, being writ to me, shall be delivered

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Even in the milk-white bosom of thy love.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: The time now serves not to expostulate.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Come, I’ll convey thee through the city-gate,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: And, ere I part with thee, confer at large

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Of all that may concern thy love affairs.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: As thou lov’st Silvia, though not for thyself,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Regard thy danger, and along with me.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: I pray thee, Lance, an if thou seest my boy,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Bid him make haste and meet me at the North Gate.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Go, sirrah, find him out. Come, Valentine.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: O, my dear Silvia! Hapless Valentine!
[_Exeunt Valentine and Proteus._]

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: I am but a fool, look you, and yet I have the wit to think my master is

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: a kind of a knave; but that’s all one if he be but one knave. He lives

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: not now that knows me to be in love, yet I am in love, but a team of

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: horse shall not pluck that from me, nor who ’tis I love; and yet ’tis a

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: woman, but what woman I will not tell myself; and yet ’tis a milkmaid;

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: yet ’tis not a maid, for she hath had gossips; yet ’tis a maid, for she

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: is her master’s maid and serves for wages. She hath more qualities than

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: a water-spaniel, which is much in a bare Christian. [_Pulls out a

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: paper_.] Here is the cate-log of her condition. _Imprimis, She can

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: fetch and carry_. Why, a horse can do no more; nay, a horse cannot

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: fetch but only carry; therefore is she better than a jade. _Item, She

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: can milk_. Look you, a sweet virtue in a maid with clean hands.
Enter Speed.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: How now, Signior Lance? What news with your mastership?

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: With my master’s ship? Why, it is at sea.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Well, your old vice still: mistake the word. What news, then, in your

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: paper?

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: The blackest news that ever thou heard’st.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Why, man? How black?

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: Why, as black as ink.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Let me read them.

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: Fie on thee, jolt-head, thou canst not read.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Thou liest. I can.

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: I will try thee. Tell me this, who begot thee?

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Marry, the son of my grandfather.

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: O, illiterate loiterer! It was the son of thy grandmother.

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: This proves that thou canst not read.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Come, fool, come; try me in thy paper.
[_Gives him the paper_.]

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: There; and Saint Nicholas be thy speed.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: _Imprimis, She can milk._

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: Ay, that she can.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: _Item, She brews good ale._

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: And thereof comes the proverb, “Blessing of your heart, you brew good

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: ale.”

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: _Item, She can sew._

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: That’s as much as to say, “Can she so?”

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: _Item, She can knit._

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: What need a man care for a stock with a wench, when she can knit him a

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: stock?

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: _Item, She can wash and scour._

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: A special virtue, for then she need not be washed and scoured.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: _Item, She can spin._

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: Then may I set the world on wheels, when she can spin for her living.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: _Item, She hath many nameless virtues._

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: That’s as much as to say, “bastard virtues”, that indeed know not their

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: fathers, and therefore have no names.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Here follow her vices.

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: Close at the heels of her virtues.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: _Item, She is not to be kissed fasting in respect of her breath._

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: Well, that fault may be mended with a breakfast.

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: Read on.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: _Item, She hath a sweet mouth._

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: That makes amends for her sour breath.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: _Item, She doth talk in her sleep._

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: It’s no matter for that, so she sleep not in her talk.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: _Item, She is slow in words._

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: O villain, that set this down among her vices! To be slow in words is a

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: woman’s only virtue. I pray thee, out with’t, and place it for her

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: chief virtue.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: _Item, She is proud._

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: Out with that too; it was Eve’s legacy and cannot be ta’en from her.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: _Item, She hath no teeth._

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: I care not for that neither, because I love crusts.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: _Item, She is curst._

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: Well, the best is, she hath no teeth to bite.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: _Item, She will often praise her liquor._

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: If her liquor be good, she shall; if she will not, I will, for good

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: things should be praised.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: _Item, She is too liberal._

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: Of her tongue she cannot, for that’s writ down she is slow of; of her

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: purse she shall not, for that I’ll keep shut. Now, of another thing she

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: may, and that cannot I help. Well, proceed.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: _Item, She hath more hair than wit, and more faults than hairs, and

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: more wealth than faults._

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: Stop there; I’ll have her. She was mine and not mine twice or thrice in

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: that last article. Rehearse that once more.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: _Item, She hath more hair than wit_—

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: More hair than wit. It may be; I’ll prove it: the cover of the salt

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: hides the salt, and therefore it is more than the salt; the hair that

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: covers the wit is more than the wit, for the greater hides the less.

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: What’s next?

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: _And more faults than hairs._

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: That’s monstrous! O, that that were out!

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: _And more wealth than faults._

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: Why, that word makes the faults gracious. Well, I’ll have her; an if it

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: be a match, as nothing is impossible—

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: What then?

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: Why, then will I tell thee that thy master stays for thee at the North

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: Gate.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: For me?

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: For thee? Ay, who art thou? He hath stayed for a better man than thee.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: And must I go to him?

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: Thou must run to him, for thou hast stayed so long that going will

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: scarce serve the turn.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Why didst not tell me sooner? Pox of your love letters!
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: Now will he be swinged for reading my letter; an unmannerly slave, that

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: will thrust himself into secrets. I’ll after, to rejoice in the boy’s

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: correction.
[_Exit._]

scenes.setting: The same. A room in the Duke’s palace

lines.text: Enter Duke and Thurio.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Sir Thurio, fear not but that she will love you

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Now Valentine is banished from her sight.

lines.speaker: THURIO
lines.text: Since his exile she hath despised me most,

lines.speaker: THURIO
lines.text: Forsworn my company and railed at me,

lines.speaker: THURIO
lines.text: That I am desperate of obtaining her.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: This weak impress of love is as a figure

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Trenched in ice, which with an hour’s heat

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Dissolves to water and doth lose his form.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: A little time will melt her frozen thoughts,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: And worthless Valentine shall be forgot.
Enter Proteus.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: How now, Sir Proteus? Is your countryman,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: According to our proclamation, gone?

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Gone, my good lord.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: My daughter takes his going grievously.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: A little time, my lord, will kill that grief.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: So I believe, but Thurio thinks not so.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Proteus, the good conceit I hold of thee,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: For thou hast shown some sign of good desert,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Makes me the better to confer with thee.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Longer than I prove loyal to your Grace

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Let me not live to look upon your Grace.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Thou know’st how willingly I would effect

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: The match between Sir Thurio and my daughter?

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: I do, my lord.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: And also, I think, thou art not ignorant

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: How she opposes her against my will?

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: She did, my lord, when Valentine was here.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Ay, and perversely she persevers so.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: What might we do to make the girl forget

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: The love of Valentine, and love Sir Thurio?

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: The best way is to slander Valentine

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: With falsehood, cowardice, and poor descent,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Three things that women highly hold in hate.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Ay, but she’ll think that it is spoke in hate.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Ay, if his enemy deliver it;

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Therefore it must with circumstance be spoken

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: By one whom she esteemeth as his friend.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Then you must undertake to slander him.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: And that, my lord, I shall be loath to do.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: ’Tis an ill office for a gentleman,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Especially against his very friend.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Where your good word cannot advantage him,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Your slander never can endamage him;

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Therefore the office is indifferent,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Being entreated to it by your friend.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: You have prevailed, my lord. If I can do it

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: By aught that I can speak in his dispraise,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: She shall not long continue love to him.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: But say this weed her love from Valentine,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: It follows not that she will love Sir Thurio.

lines.speaker: THURIO
lines.text: Therefore, as you unwind her love from him,

lines.speaker: THURIO
lines.text: Lest it should ravel and be good to none,

lines.speaker: THURIO
lines.text: You must provide to bottom it on me,

lines.speaker: THURIO
lines.text: Which must be done by praising me as much

lines.speaker: THURIO
lines.text: As you in worth dispraise Sir Valentine.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: And, Proteus, we dare trust you in this kind

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Because we know, on Valentine’s report,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: You are already Love’s firm votary

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: And cannot soon revolt and change your mind.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Upon this warrant shall you have access

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Where you with Silvia may confer at large—

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: For she is lumpish, heavy, melancholy,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: And, for your friend’s sake, will be glad of you—

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Where you may temper her by your persuasion

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: To hate young Valentine and love my friend.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: As much as I can do I will effect.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: But you, Sir Thurio, are not sharp enough.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: You must lay lime to tangle her desires

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: By wailful sonnets, whose composed rhymes

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Should be full-fraught with serviceable vows.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Ay, much is the force of heaven-bred poesy.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Say that upon the altar of her beauty

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: You sacrifice your tears, your sighs, your heart.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Write till your ink be dry, and with your tears

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Moist it again, and frame some feeling line

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: That may discover such integrity.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: For Orpheus’ lute was strung with poets’ sinews,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Whose golden touch could soften steel and stones,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Make tigers tame, and huge leviathans

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Forsake unsounded deeps to dance on sands.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: After your dire-lamenting elegies,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Visit by night your lady’s chamber-window

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: With some sweet consort; to their instruments

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Tune a deploring dump; the night’s dead silence

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Will well become such sweet-complaining grievance.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: This, or else nothing, will inherit her.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: This discipline shows thou hast been in love.

lines.speaker: THURIO
lines.text: And thy advice this night I’ll put in practice.

lines.speaker: THURIO
lines.text: Therefore, sweet Proteus, my direction-giver,

lines.speaker: THURIO
lines.text: Let us into the city presently

lines.speaker: THURIO
lines.text: To sort some gentlemen well skilled in music.

lines.speaker: THURIO
lines.text: I have a sonnet that will serve the turn

lines.speaker: THURIO
lines.text: To give the onset to thy good advice.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: About it, gentlemen!

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: We’ll wait upon your Grace till after supper,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: And afterward determine our proceedings.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Even now about it! I will pardon you.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: A forest between Milan and Verona

lines.text: Enter certain Outlaws.

lines.speaker: FIRST OUTLAW
lines.text: Fellows, stand fast. I see a passenger.

lines.speaker: SECOND OUTLAW
lines.text: If there be ten, shrink not, but down with ’em.
Enter Valentine and Speed.

lines.speaker: THIRD OUTLAW
lines.text: Stand, sir, and throw us that you have about ye.

lines.speaker: THIRD OUTLAW
lines.text: If not, we’ll make you sit, and rifle you.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Sir, we are undone: these are the villains

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: That all the travellers do fear so much.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: My friends—

lines.speaker: FIRST OUTLAW
lines.text: That’s not so, sir. We are your enemies.

lines.speaker: SECOND OUTLAW
lines.text: Peace! We’ll hear him.

lines.speaker: THIRD OUTLAW
lines.text: Ay, by my beard, will we, for he is a proper man.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Then know that I have little wealth to lose.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: A man I am crossed with adversity;

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: My riches are these poor habiliments,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Of which if you should here disfurnish me,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: You take the sum and substance that I have.

lines.speaker: SECOND OUTLAW
lines.text: Whither travel you?

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: To Verona.

lines.speaker: FIRST OUTLAW
lines.text: Whence came you?

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: From Milan.

lines.speaker: THIRD OUTLAW
lines.text: Have you long sojourned there?

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Some sixteen months, and longer might have stayed

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: If crooked fortune had not thwarted me.

lines.speaker: FIRST OUTLAW
lines.text: What, were you banished thence?

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: I was.

lines.speaker: SECOND OUTLAW
lines.text: For what offence?

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: For that which now torments me to rehearse;

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: I killed a man, whose death I much repent,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: But yet I slew him manfully in fight,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Without false vantage or base treachery.

lines.speaker: FIRST OUTLAW
lines.text: Why, ne’er repent it, if it were done so.

lines.speaker: FIRST OUTLAW
lines.text: But were you banished for so small a fault?

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: I was, and held me glad of such a doom.

lines.speaker: SECOND OUTLAW
lines.text: Have you the tongues?

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: My youthful travel therein made me happy,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Or else I often had been miserable.

lines.speaker: THIRD OUTLAW
lines.text: By the bare scalp of Robin Hood’s fat friar,

lines.speaker: THIRD OUTLAW
lines.text: This fellow were a king for our wild faction.

lines.speaker: FIRST OUTLAW
lines.text: We’ll have him. Sirs, a word.

lines.speaker: SPEED
lines.text: Master, be one of them. It’s an honourable kind of thievery.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Peace, villain.

lines.speaker: SECOND OUTLAW
lines.text: Tell us this: have you anything to take to?

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Nothing but my fortune.

lines.speaker: THIRD OUTLAW
lines.text: Know then that some of us are gentlemen,

lines.speaker: THIRD OUTLAW
lines.text: Such as the fury of ungoverned youth

lines.speaker: THIRD OUTLAW
lines.text: Thrust from the company of awful men.

lines.speaker: THIRD OUTLAW
lines.text: Myself was from Verona banished

lines.speaker: THIRD OUTLAW
lines.text: For practising to steal away a lady,

lines.speaker: THIRD OUTLAW
lines.text: An heir, and near allied unto the Duke.

lines.speaker: SECOND OUTLAW
lines.text: And I from Mantua, for a gentleman

lines.speaker: SECOND OUTLAW
lines.text: Who, in my mood, I stabbed unto the heart.

lines.speaker: FIRST OUTLAW
lines.text: And I for suchlike petty crimes as these.

lines.speaker: FIRST OUTLAW
lines.text: But to the purpose, for we cite our faults,

lines.speaker: FIRST OUTLAW
lines.text: That they may hold excused our lawless lives;

lines.speaker: FIRST OUTLAW
lines.text: And partly, seeing you are beautified

lines.speaker: FIRST OUTLAW
lines.text: With goodly shape, and by your own report

lines.speaker: FIRST OUTLAW
lines.text: A linguist, and a man of such perfection

lines.speaker: FIRST OUTLAW
lines.text: As we do in our quality much want—

lines.speaker: SECOND OUTLAW
lines.text: Indeed because you are a banished man,

lines.speaker: SECOND OUTLAW
lines.text: Therefore, above the rest, we parley to you.

lines.speaker: SECOND OUTLAW
lines.text: Are you content to be our general?

lines.speaker: SECOND OUTLAW
lines.text: To make a virtue of necessity

lines.speaker: SECOND OUTLAW
lines.text: And live as we do in this wilderness?

lines.speaker: THIRD OUTLAW
lines.text: What sayst thou? Wilt thou be of our consort?

lines.speaker: THIRD OUTLAW
lines.text: Say “Ay”, and be the captain of us all,

lines.speaker: THIRD OUTLAW
lines.text: We’ll do thee homage and be ruled by thee,

lines.speaker: THIRD OUTLAW
lines.text: Love thee as our commander and our king.

lines.speaker: FIRST OUTLAW
lines.text: But if thou scorn our courtesy, thou diest.

lines.speaker: SECOND OUTLAW
lines.text: Thou shalt not live to brag what we have offered.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: I take your offer and will live with you,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Provided that you do no outrages

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: On silly women or poor passengers.

lines.speaker: THIRD OUTLAW
lines.text: No, we detest such vile base practices.

lines.speaker: THIRD OUTLAW
lines.text: Come, go with us; we’ll bring thee to our crews

lines.speaker: THIRD OUTLAW
lines.text: And show thee all the treasure we have got,

lines.speaker: THIRD OUTLAW
lines.text: Which, with ourselves, all rest at thy dispose.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: Milan. The court of the Duke’s palace

lines.text: Enter Proteus.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Already have I been false to Valentine,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: And now I must be as unjust to Thurio.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Under the colour of commending him,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: I have access my own love to prefer.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: But Silvia is too fair, too true, too holy

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: To be corrupted with my worthless gifts.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: When I protest true loyalty to her,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: She twits me with my falsehood to my friend;

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: When to her beauty I commend my vows,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: She bids me think how I have been forsworn

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: In breaking faith with Julia, whom I loved;

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: And notwithstanding all her sudden quips,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: The least whereof would quell a lover’s hope,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Yet, spaniel-like, the more she spurns my love,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: The more it grows and fawneth on her still.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: But here comes Thurio. Now must we to her window,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: And give some evening music to her ear.
Enter Thurio and Musicians.

lines.speaker: THURIO
lines.text: How now, Sir Proteus, are you crept before us?

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Ay, gentle Thurio, for you know that love

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Will creep in service where it cannot go.

lines.speaker: THURIO
lines.text: Ay, but I hope, sir, that you love not here.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Sir, but I do, or else I would be hence.

lines.speaker: THURIO
lines.text: Who? Silvia?

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Ay, Silvia, for your sake.

lines.speaker: THURIO
lines.text: I thank you for your own. Now, gentlemen,

lines.speaker: THURIO
lines.text: Let’s tune, and to it lustily awhile.
Enter Host and Julia in boy’s clothes, as Sebastian.

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: Now, my young guest, methinks you’re allycholly. I pray you, why is it?

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Marry, mine host, because I cannot be merry.

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: Come, we’ll have you merry. I’ll bring you where you shall hear music,

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: and see the gentleman that you asked for.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: But shall I hear him speak?

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: Ay, that you shall.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: That will be music.
[_Music plays._]

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: Hark, hark!

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Is he among these?

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: Ay; but peace, let’s hear ’em.

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: SONG

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Who is Silvia? What is she,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: That all our swains commend her?

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Holy, fair, and wise is she;

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: The heaven such grace did lend her,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: That she might admired be.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Is she kind as she is fair?

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: For beauty lives with kindness.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Love doth to her eyes repair,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: To help him of his blindness;

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: And, being helped, inhabits there.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Then to Silvia let us sing,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: That Silvia is excelling;

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: She excels each mortal thing

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Upon the dull earth dwelling.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: To her let us garlands bring.

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: How now, are you sadder than you were before?

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: How do you, man? The music likes you not.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: You mistake; the musician likes me not.

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: Why, my pretty youth?

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: He plays false, father.

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: How, out of tune on the strings?

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Not so; but yet so false that he grieves my very heart-strings.

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: You have a quick ear.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Ay, I would I were deaf; it makes me have a slow heart.

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: I perceive you delight not in music.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Not a whit, when it jars so.

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: Hark, what fine change is in the music!

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Ay, that change is the spite.

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: You would have them always play but one thing?

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: I would always have one play but one thing.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: But, host, doth this Sir Proteus, that we talk on,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Often resort unto this gentlewoman?

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: I tell you what Lance, his man, told me: he loved her out of all nick.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Where is Lance?

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: Gone to seek his dog, which tomorrow, by his master’s command, he must

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: carry for a present to his lady.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Peace, stand aside. The company parts.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Sir Thurio, fear not you; I will so plead

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: That you shall say my cunning drift excels.

lines.speaker: THURIO
lines.text: Where meet we?

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: At Saint Gregory’s well.

lines.speaker: THURIO
lines.text: Farewell.
[_Exeunt Thurio and Musicians._]
Enter Silvia above.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Madam, good even to your ladyship.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: I thank you for your music, gentlemen.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Who is that that spake?

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: One, lady, if you knew his pure heart’s truth,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: You would quickly learn to know him by his voice.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Sir Proteus, as I take it.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Sir Proteus, gentle lady, and your servant.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: What’s your will?

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: That I may compass yours.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: You have your wish. My will is even this,

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: That presently you hie you home to bed.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Thou subtle, perjured, false, disloyal man,

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Think’st thou I am so shallow, so conceitless,

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: To be seduced by thy flattery,

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: That hast deceived so many with thy vows?

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Return, return, and make thy love amends.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: For me, by this pale queen of night I swear,

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: I am so far from granting thy request

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: That I despise thee for thy wrongful suit,

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: And by and by intend to chide myself

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Even for this time I spend in talking to thee.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: I grant, sweet love, that I did love a lady,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: But she is dead.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: ’Twere false, if I should speak it,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: For I am sure she is not buried.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Say that she be; yet Valentine thy friend

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Survives, to whom, thyself art witness,

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: I am betrothed. And art thou not ashamed

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: To wrong him with thy importunacy?

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: I likewise hear that Valentine is dead.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: And so suppose am I, for in his grave,

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Assure thyself, my love is buried.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Sweet lady, let me rake it from the earth.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Go to thy lady’s grave and call hers thence,

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Or, at the least, in hers sepulchre thine.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: He heard not that.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Madam, if your heart be so obdurate,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Vouchsafe me yet your picture for my love,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: The picture that is hanging in your chamber;

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: To that I’ll speak, to that I’ll sigh and weep;

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: For since the substance of your perfect self

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Is else devoted, I am but a shadow;

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: And to your shadow will I make true love.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: If ’twere a substance you would sure deceive it

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: And make it but a shadow, as I am.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: I am very loath to be your idol, sir;

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: But since your falsehood shall become you well

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: To worship shadows and adore false shapes,

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Send to me in the morning, and I’ll send it.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: And so, good rest.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: As wretches have o’ernight

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: That wait for execution in the morn.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Host, will you go?

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: By my halidom, I was fast asleep.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Pray you, where lies Sir Proteus?

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: Marry, at my house. Trust me, I think ’tis almost day.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Not so; but it hath been the longest night

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: That e’er I watched, and the most heaviest.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: The same

lines.text: Enter Eglamour.

lines.speaker: EGLAMOUR
lines.text: This is the hour that Madam Silvia

lines.speaker: EGLAMOUR
lines.text: Entreated me to call and know her mind;

lines.speaker: EGLAMOUR
lines.text: There’s some great matter she’d employ me in.

lines.speaker: EGLAMOUR
lines.text: Madam, madam!
Enter Silvia above.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Who calls?

lines.speaker: EGLAMOUR
lines.text: Your servant and your friend;

lines.speaker: EGLAMOUR
lines.text: One that attends your ladyship’s command.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Sir Eglamour, a thousand times good morrow.

lines.speaker: EGLAMOUR
lines.text: As many, worthy lady, to yourself.

lines.speaker: EGLAMOUR
lines.text: According to your ladyship’s impose,

lines.speaker: EGLAMOUR
lines.text: I am thus early come to know what service

lines.speaker: EGLAMOUR
lines.text: It is your pleasure to command me in.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: O Eglamour, thou art a gentleman—

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Think not I flatter, for I swear I do not—

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Valiant, wise, remorseful, well accomplished.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Thou art not ignorant what dear good will

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: I bear unto the banished Valentine,

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Nor how my father would enforce me marry

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Vain Thurio, whom my very soul abhorred.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Thyself hast loved, and I have heard thee say

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: No grief did ever come so near thy heart

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: As when thy lady and thy true love died,

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Upon whose grave thou vowed’st pure chastity.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Sir Eglamour, I would to Valentine,

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: To Mantua, where I hear he makes abode;

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: And for the ways are dangerous to pass,

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: I do desire thy worthy company,

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Upon whose faith and honour I repose.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Urge not my father’s anger, Eglamour,

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: But think upon my grief, a lady’s grief,

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: And on the justice of my flying hence

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: To keep me from a most unholy match,

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Which heaven and fortune still rewards with plagues.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: I do desire thee, even from a heart

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: As full of sorrows as the sea of sands,

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: To bear me company and go with me;

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: If not, to hide what I have said to thee,

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: That I may venture to depart alone.

lines.speaker: EGLAMOUR
lines.text: Madam, I pity much your grievances,

lines.speaker: EGLAMOUR
lines.text: Which, since I know they virtuously are placed,

lines.speaker: EGLAMOUR
lines.text: I give consent to go along with you,

lines.speaker: EGLAMOUR
lines.text: Recking as little what betideth me

lines.speaker: EGLAMOUR
lines.text: As much I wish all good befortune you.

lines.speaker: EGLAMOUR
lines.text: When will you go?

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: This evening coming.

lines.speaker: EGLAMOUR
lines.text: Where shall I meet you?

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: At Friar Patrick’s cell,

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Where I intend holy confession.

lines.speaker: EGLAMOUR
lines.text: I will not fail your ladyship. Good morrow, gentle lady.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Good morrow, kind Sir Eglamour.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: The same

lines.text: Enter Lance with his dog Crab.

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: When a man’s servant shall play the cur with him, look you, it goes

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: hard: one that I brought up of a puppy; one that I saved from drowning

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: when three or four of his blind brothers and sisters went to it. I have

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: taught him even as one would say precisely, “Thus I would teach a dog.”

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: I was sent to deliver him as a present to Mistress Silvia from my

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: master; and I came no sooner into the dining-chamber but he steps me to

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: her trencher and steals her capon’s leg. O, ’tis a foul thing when a

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: cur cannot keep himself in all companies! I would have, as one should

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: say, one that takes upon him to be a dog indeed, to be, as it were, a

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: dog at all things. If I had not had more wit than he, to take a fault

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: upon me that he did, I think verily he had been hanged for’t; sure as I

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: live, he had suffered for’t. You shall judge. He thrusts me himself

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: into the company of three or four gentleman-like dogs under the Duke’s

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: table; he had not been there—bless the mark!—a pissing-while but all

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: the chamber smelt him. “Out with the dog!” says one; “What cur is

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: that?” says another; “Whip him out”, says the third; “Hang him up”,

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: says the Duke. I, having been acquainted with the smell before, knew it

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: was Crab, and goes me to the fellow that whips the dogs. “Friend,”

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: quoth I, “you mean to whip the dog?” “Ay, marry do I,” quoth he. “You do

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: him the more wrong,” quoth I. “’Twas I did the thing you wot of.” He

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: makes me no more ado but whips me out of the chamber. How many masters

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: would do this for his servant? Nay, I’ll be sworn I have sat in the

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: stock for puddings he hath stolen, otherwise he had been executed. I

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: have stood on the pillory for geese he hath killed, otherwise he had

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: suffered for’t. [_To Crab_.] Thou think’st not of this now. Nay, I

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: remember the trick you served me when I took my leave of Madam Silvia.

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: Did not I bid thee still mark me, and do as I do? When didst thou see

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: me heave up my leg and make water against a gentlewoman’s farthingale?

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: Didst thou ever see me do such a trick?
Enter Proteus and Julia disguised as Sebastian.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Sebastian is thy name? I like thee well,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: And will employ thee in some service presently.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: In what you please; I’ll do what I can.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: I hope thou wilt. [_To Lance_.] How now, you whoreson peasant,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Where have you been these two days loitering?

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: Marry, sir, I carried Mistress Silvia the dog you bade me.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: And what says she to my little jewel?

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: Marry, she says your dog was a cur, and tells you currish thanks is

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: good enough for such a present.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: But she received my dog?

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: No, indeed, did she not. Here have I brought him back again.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: What, didst thou offer her this from me?

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: Ay, sir, the other squirrel was stolen from me by the hangman’s boys in

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: the market-place, and then I offered her mine own, who is a dog as big

lines.speaker: LANCE
lines.text: as ten of yours, and therefore the gift the greater.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Go, get thee hence, and find my dog again,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Or ne’er return again into my sight.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Away, I say. Stayest thou to vex me here?

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: A slave that still an end turns me to shame.
[_Exit Lance with Crab._]

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Sebastian, I have entertained thee

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Partly that I have need of such a youth

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: That can with some discretion do my business—

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: For ’tis no trusting to yond foolish lout—

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: But chiefly for thy face and thy behaviour,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Which, if my augury deceive me not,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Witness good bringing up, fortune, and truth.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Therefore, know thou, for this I entertain thee.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Go presently, and take this ring with thee,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Deliver it to Madam Silvia.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: She loved me well delivered it to me.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: It seems you loved not her, to leave her token.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: She’s dead belike?

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Not so; I think she lives.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Alas!

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Why dost thou cry “Alas”?

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: I cannot choose

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: But pity her.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Wherefore shouldst thou pity her?

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Because methinks that she loved you as well

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: As you do love your lady Silvia.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: She dreams on him that has forgot her love;

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: You dote on her that cares not for your love.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: ’Tis pity love should be so contrary;

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: And thinking on it makes me cry “Alas.”

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Well, give her that ring, and therewithal

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: This letter. That’s her chamber. Tell my lady

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: I claim the promise for her heavenly picture.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Your message done, hie home unto my chamber,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Where thou shalt find me sad and solitary.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: How many women would do such a message?

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Alas, poor Proteus, thou hast entertained

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: A fox to be the shepherd of thy lambs.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Alas, poor fool, why do I pity him

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: That with his very heart despiseth me?

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Because he loves her, he despiseth me;

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Because I love him, I must pity him.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: This ring I gave him when he parted from me,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: To bind him to remember my good will;

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: And now am I, unhappy messenger,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: To plead for that which I would not obtain,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: To carry that which I would have refused,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: To praise his faith, which I would have dispraised.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: I am my master’s true confirmed love,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: But cannot be true servant to my master

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Unless I prove false traitor to myself.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Yet will I woo for him, but yet so coldly

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: As, heaven it knows, I would not have him speed.
Enter Silvia attended.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Gentlewoman, good day. I pray you be my mean

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: To bring me where to speak with Madam Silvia.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: What would you with her, if that I be she?

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: If you be she, I do entreat your patience

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: To hear me speak the message I am sent on.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: From whom?

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: From my master, Sir Proteus, madam.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: O, he sends you for a picture?

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Ay, madam.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Ursula, bring my picture there.
[_She is brought the picture._]

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Go, give your master this. Tell him from me,

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: One Julia, that his changing thoughts forget,

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Would better fit his chamber than this shadow.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Madam, please you peruse this letter.
[_Gives her a letter._]

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Pardon me, madam, I have unadvised

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Delivered you a paper that I should not.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: This is the letter to your ladyship.
[_Takes back the letter and gives her another._]

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: I pray thee, let me look on that again.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: It may not be. Good madam, pardon me.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: There, hold.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: I will not look upon your master’s lines.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: I know they are stuffed with protestations

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: And full of new-found oaths, which he will break

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: As easily as I do tear his paper.
[_She tears the second letter._]

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Madam, he sends your ladyship this ring.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: The more shame for him that he sends it me;

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: For I have heard him say a thousand times

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: His Julia gave it him at his departure.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Though his false finger have profaned the ring,

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Mine shall not do his Julia so much wrong.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: She thanks you.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: What sayst thou?

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: I thank you, madam, that you tender her.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Poor gentlewoman, my master wrongs her much.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Dost thou know her?

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Almost as well as I do know myself.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: To think upon her woes, I do protest

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: That I have wept a hundred several times.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Belike she thinks that Proteus hath forsook her?

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: I think she doth, and that’s her cause of sorrow.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Is she not passing fair?

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: She hath been fairer, madam, than she is.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: When she did think my master loved her well,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: She, in my judgement, was as fair as you.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: But since she did neglect her looking-glass

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: And threw her sun-expelling mask away,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: The air hath starved the roses in her cheeks

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: And pinched the lily-tincture of her face,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: That now she is become as black as I.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: How tall was she?

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: About my stature; for at Pentecost,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: When all our pageants of delight were played,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Our youth got me to play the woman’s part,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: And I was trimmed in Madam Julia’s gown,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Which served me as fit, by all men’s judgements,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: As if the garment had been made for me;

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Therefore I know she is about my height.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: And at that time I made her weep agood,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: For I did play a lamentable part.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Madam, ’twas Ariadne, passioning

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: For Theseus’ perjury and unjust flight,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Which I so lively acted with my tears

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: That my poor mistress, moved therewithal,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Wept bitterly; and would I might be dead

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: If I in thought felt not her very sorrow.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: She is beholding to thee, gentle youth.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Alas, poor lady, desolate and left!

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: I weep myself to think upon thy words.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Here, youth, there is my purse. I give thee this

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: For thy sweet mistress’ sake, because thou lov’st her.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Farewell.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: And she shall thank you for’t, if e’er you know her.
[_Exeunt Silvia and Attendants._]

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: A virtuous gentlewoman, mild and beautiful.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: I hope my master’s suit will be but cold,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Since she respects my mistress’ love so much.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Alas, how love can trifle with itself!

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Here is her picture; let me see. I think

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: If I had such a tire, this face of mine

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Were full as lovely as is this of hers;

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: And yet the painter flattered her a little,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Unless I flatter with myself too much.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Her hair is auburn, mine is perfect yellow;

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: If that be all the difference in his love,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: I’ll get me such a coloured periwig.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Her eyes are grey as glass, and so are mine.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Ay, but her forehead’s low, and mine’s as high.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: What should it be that he respects in her

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: But I can make respective in myself,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: If this fond Love were not a blinded god?

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Come, shadow, come, and take this shadow up,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: For ’tis thy rival. O thou senseless form,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Thou shalt be worshipped, kissed, loved, and adored;

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: And were there sense in his idolatry,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: My substance should be statue in thy stead.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: I’ll use thee kindly for thy mistress’ sake,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: That used me so; or else, by Jove I vow,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: I should have scratched out your unseeing eyes

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: To make my master out of love with thee.
[_Exit._]

scenes.setting: Milan. An abbey

lines.text: Enter Eglamour.

lines.speaker: EGLAMOUR
lines.text: The sun begins to gild the western sky,

lines.speaker: EGLAMOUR
lines.text: And now it is about the very hour

lines.speaker: EGLAMOUR
lines.text: That Silvia at Friar Patrick’s cell should meet me.

lines.speaker: EGLAMOUR
lines.text: She will not fail, for lovers break not hours,

lines.speaker: EGLAMOUR
lines.text: Unless it be to come before their time,

lines.speaker: EGLAMOUR
lines.text: So much they spur their expedition.
Enter Silvia.

lines.speaker: EGLAMOUR
lines.text: See where she comes. Lady, a happy evening!

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Amen, amen. Go on, good Eglamour,

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Out at the postern by the abbey wall.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: I fear I am attended by some spies.

lines.speaker: EGLAMOUR
lines.text: Fear not. The forest is not three leagues off;

lines.speaker: EGLAMOUR
lines.text: If we recover that, we are sure enough.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: The same. A room in the Duke’s palace

lines.text: Enter Thurio, Proteus and Julia.

lines.speaker: THURIO
lines.text: Sir Proteus, what says Silvia to my suit?

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: O, sir, I find her milder than she was,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: And yet she takes exceptions at your person.

lines.speaker: THURIO
lines.text: What? That my leg is too long?

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: No, that it is too little.

lines.speaker: THURIO
lines.text: I’ll wear a boot to make it somewhat rounder.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: But love will not be spurred to what it loathes.

lines.speaker: THURIO
lines.text: What says she to my face?

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: She says it is a fair one.

lines.speaker: THURIO
lines.text: Nay, then, the wanton lies; my face is black.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: But pearls are fair; and the old saying is,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: “Black men are pearls in beauteous ladies’ eyes.”
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: ’Tis true, such pearls as put out ladies’ eyes,

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: For I had rather wink than look on them.

lines.speaker: THURIO
lines.text: How likes she my discourse?

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Ill, when you talk of war.

lines.speaker: THURIO
lines.text: But well when I discourse of love and peace.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: But better, indeed, when you hold your peace.

lines.speaker: THURIO
lines.text: What says she to my valour?

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: O, sir, she makes no doubt of that.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: She needs not, when she knows it cowardice.

lines.speaker: THURIO
lines.text: What says she to my birth?

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: That you are well derived.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: True, from a gentleman to a fool.

lines.speaker: THURIO
lines.text: Considers she my possessions?

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: O, ay, and pities them.

lines.speaker: THURIO
lines.text: Wherefore?
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: That such an ass should owe them.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: That they are out by lease.

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Here comes the Duke.
Enter Duke.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: How now, Sir Proteus! How now, Thurio!

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Which of you saw Sir Eglamour of late?

lines.speaker: THURIO
lines.text: Not I.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Nor I.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Saw you my daughter?

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Neither.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Why then, she’s fled unto that peasant Valentine,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: And Eglamour is in her company.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: ’Tis true, for Friar Lawrence met them both

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: As he in penance wandered through the forest;

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Him he knew well, and guessed that it was she,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: But, being masked, he was not sure of it.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Besides, she did intend confession

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: At Patrick’s cell this even, and there she was not.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: These likelihoods confirm her flight from hence.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Therefore, I pray you, stand not to discourse,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: But mount you presently and meet with me

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Upon the rising of the mountain foot

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: That leads toward Mantua, whither they are fled.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Dispatch, sweet gentlemen, and follow me.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: THURIO
lines.text: Why, this it is to be a peevish girl

lines.speaker: THURIO
lines.text: That flies her fortune when it follows her.

lines.speaker: THURIO
lines.text: I’ll after, more to be revenged on Eglamour

lines.speaker: THURIO
lines.text: Than for the love of reckless Silvia.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: And I will follow, more for Silvia’s love

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Than hate of Eglamour that goes with her.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: And I will follow, more to cross that love

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: Than hate for Silvia, that is gone for love.
[_Exit._]

scenes.setting: Frontiers of Mantua. The forest

lines.text: Enter Silvia and Outlaws.

lines.speaker: FIRST OUTLAW
lines.text: Come, come, be patient. We must bring you to our captain.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: A thousand more mischances than this one

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Have learned me how to brook this patiently.

lines.speaker: SECOND OUTLAW
lines.text: Come, bring her away.

lines.speaker: FIRST OUTLAW
lines.text: Where is the gentleman that was with her?

lines.speaker: SECOND OUTLAW
lines.text: Being nimble-footed, he hath outrun us.

lines.speaker: SECOND OUTLAW
lines.text: But Moyses and Valerius follow him.

lines.speaker: SECOND OUTLAW
lines.text: Go thou with her to the west end of the wood;

lines.speaker: SECOND OUTLAW
lines.text: There is our captain. We’ll follow him that’s fled.

lines.speaker: SECOND OUTLAW
lines.text: The thicket is beset; he cannot ’scape.
[_Exeunt Second and Third Outlaws._]

lines.speaker: FIRST OUTLAW
lines.text: Come, I must bring you to our captain’s cave.

lines.speaker: FIRST OUTLAW
lines.text: Fear not; he bears an honourable mind

lines.speaker: FIRST OUTLAW
lines.text: And will not use a woman lawlessly.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: O Valentine, this I endure for thee!
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: Another part of the forest

lines.text: Enter Valentine.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: How use doth breed a habit in a man!

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: This shadowy desert, unfrequented woods,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: I better brook than flourishing peopled towns.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Here can I sit alone, unseen of any,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: And to the nightingale’s complaining notes

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Tune my distresses and record my woes.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: O thou that dost inhabit in my breast,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Leave not the mansion so long tenantless,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Lest, growing ruinous, the building fall

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: And leave no memory of what it was.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Repair me with thy presence, Silvia;

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Thou gentle nymph, cherish thy forlorn swain.
[_Shouts within._]

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: What hallowing and what stir is this today?

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: These are my mates, that make their wills their law,

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Have some unhappy passenger in chase.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: They love me well; yet I have much to do

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: To keep them from uncivil outrages.

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Withdraw thee, Valentine. Who’s this comes here?
[_Steps aside._]
Enter Proteus, Silvia and Julia as Sebastian.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Madam, this service I have done for you—

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Though you respect not aught your servant doth—

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: To hazard life, and rescue you from him

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: That would have forced your honour and your love.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Vouchsafe me for my meed but one fair look;

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: A smaller boon than this I cannot beg,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: And less than this, I am sure, you cannot give.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: How like a dream is this I see and hear!

lines.speaker: VALENTINE
lines.text: Love, lend me patience to forbear awhile.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: O miserable, unhappy that I am!

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Unhappy were you, madam, ere I came;

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: But by my coming I have made you happy.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: By thy approach thou mak’st me most unhappy.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: JULIA
lines.text: And me, when he approacheth to your presence.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Had I been seized by a hungry lion,

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: I would have been a breakfast to the beast

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Rather than have false Proteus rescue me.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: O heaven, be judge how I love Valentine,

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Whose life’s as tender to me as my soul!

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: And full as much, for more there cannot be,

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: I do detest false perjured Proteus.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Therefore be gone, solicit me no more.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: What dangerous action, stood it next to death,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Would I not undergo for one calm look!

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: O, ’tis the curse in love, and still approved,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: When women cannot love where they’re beloved.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: When Proteus cannot love where he’s beloved.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Read over Julia’s heart, thy first best love,

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: For whose dear sake thou didst then rend thy faith

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Into a thousand oaths; and all those oaths

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Descended into perjury to love me.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Thou hast no faith left now, unless thou’dst two,

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: And that’s far worse than none; better have none

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Than plural faith, which is too much by one.

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: Thou counterfeit to thy true friend!

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: In love

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Who respects friend?

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: All men but Proteus.

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Nay, if the gentle spirit of moving words

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: Can no way change you to a milder form,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: I’ll woo you like a soldier, at arms’ end,

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
lines.text: And love you ’gainst the nature of love—force ye.
[_He seizes her._]

lines.speaker: SILVIA
lines.text: O heaven!

lines.speaker: PROTEUS
